lessons.title: Building an AI Script
lessons.content_md:
# The Capstone Project 🏆

You've learned how AI works. Now it's time to actually use it. We are going to write a Python script that calls a real AI API (like Google Gemini or OpenAI) and push the code to GitHub.

## Step 1: Get Your API Key

First, you need an **API Key**. This is a secret password that allows your code to talk to the AI provider's servers. Go to the provider's developer console and generate a free API key.

<flipcard front="🔑 What is an API Key?" back="A unique string of characters used to authenticate your script so the AI provider knows who is making the request."></flipcard>

## Step 2: Write the Python Code

Create a new file called `ai_assistant.py` and install the provider's Python library (e.g., `pip install google-genai`).

Write a simple script that asks the AI a question:

```python
import os
from google import genai

client = genai.Client(api_key=os.environ.get("GEMINI_API_KEY"))

response = client.models.generate_content(
    model='gemini-2.5-flash',
    contents='Explain Quantum Computing to a 5 year old.',
)

print(response.text)
```

## Step 3: Secure Your Key

**NEVER** paste your API key directly into your code if you are going to put it on the internet. Hackers will steal it. Instead, save it as an Environment Variable on your computer.

<flipcard front="🛑 What happens if I put my API Key on GitHub?" back="Bots constantly scan GitHub for exposed keys. They will steal yours and run up thousands of dollars in server charges on your account!"></flipcard>

## Step 4: Push to GitHub

Initialize a git repository, commit your code, and push it to your GitHub profile to show the world what you've built!

<flipcard front="🚀 Congratulations!" back="You have successfully completed the AI & Machine Learning Track. You are now ready to build intelligent applications!"></flipcard>
